text:
Marcus: FYI — after yesterday's AWQ calibration sweep on qwen-7b we see ~12% p50 latency regression and a small token-throughput drop. Traces point at KV prefetch churn + kernel-selection thrash.
Devon: ugh. which commit/runner? can you paste the perf profile and the exact model config?
Marcus: running on dedicated-prod pool, commit 8f3a2c4. model: qwen-7b-awq-v2 (rope-scale=1.0, heads=16, kv-dim=128). perf command I used:
```
./rbench --model qwen-7b-awq-v2 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --profile --kernels=auto --kv-prefetch=on
```
Marcus: profiler snippet:
```
SUMMARY: tokens/s=27.4, p50=82ms, p95=210ms
KERNEL SELECTION: fast_gemm: 46% 
                 generic_attn: 38% 
                 fallback_copy: 9% 
KV CACHE: hits=0.71, evict_rate=0.12, avg_fetch_ms=3.8
```
Anya: what were the calibration prompts? AWQ can shift activation ranges; if calibration set is shorter/biased we might trigger different kernels for long seqs.
Marcus: used the standard calib set from infra: `awq_calib_v4.txt` (mostly short QA pairs). I suspect distribution mismatch vs production long-context chats.
Devon: that could explain the generic_attn spike on long seqs. When AWQ quant changes the op shapes, the kernel selector might prefer a slower path for safety. Can you repro locally with `--force-kernel=fast_gemm` vs `--force-kernel=generic_attn`?
Marcus: did that quickly: forcing `fast_gemm` restores p50 to ~73ms, tokens/s=29.0. forcing `generic_attn` matches the regression numbers. Forcing `fast_gemm` also increases memory ~200MB.
Olivia: sounds like kernel selector heuristics are mis-ranking the AWQ variant for certain sequence-length distributions. Two angles: (1) adjust selector cost model to include quantized kernel benefits for AWQ, (2) change calib to include longer sequences so AWQ doesn't push kernels to generic.
Anya: also verify RoPE scaling. If rope-scale != training, attention math changes and some optimized kernels bail out. Marcus, what's rope-scale in the AWQ build?
Marcus: rope-scale=1.0 (we didn't touch it). But Mistral/Mixtral runs earlier with rope-scale tweaks showed similar kernel fallbacks.
Devon: hypothesis: head/kv dim mismatch at runtime after quantization triggers extra transposes/copies -> fallback_copy time. Check `kernel_trace` with timestamps for transpose ops.
Marcus: attached short trace lines below:
```
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] select_kernel fast_gemm (score=12.3)
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] select_kernel generic_attn (score=12.5) <-- chosen
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] transpose_kv 1.9ms
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] kv_fetch 3.6ms
[2026-11-02T09:12:34Z] fallback_copy 6.4ms
```
Anya: that 0.2 score delta is tiny; suggests our selector has numeric instability. Might be rounding differences in AWQ quant that change micro-benchmarks. We should add a hysteresis window to avoid flipping kernels mid-request.
Olivia: agree. Also want to run an experiment: out-of-band compare AWQ vs GPTQ int8 kernels for qwen-7b on long sequences and the official eval prompts to measure accuracy delta. If GPTQ keeps fast kernels with minor accuracy loss, it may be acceptable as a fallback.
Marcus: ran quick eval on 200 prompt subset: AWQ delta vs float: +0.8% token-level perplexity; GPTQ int8 delta: +1.1%. AWQ slightly better accuracy but slower due to kernel choice.
Devon: cost/perf tradeoff. Could implement runtime policy: prefer AWQ unless kernel score predicts a generic path, then automatically route to GPTQ-int8 variant. That keeps accuracy when fast kernels available and avoids regressions.
Anya: need to be careful — switching model variants mid-request is risky for long chats because of KV/format differences. But we can route per-request at start. Add a candidate check: simulate selector on a short prefix to predict path.
perf-bot: Alert created #perf-regress-1972345678 linking thread. Attached perf diffs and heap snapshots.
Olivia: actionable plan:
- Marcus: run `--kernel-trace` across a wider seq distribution (done by EOD).
- Devon: add hysteresis logic to selector (PR idea sketched).
- Anya: re-run AWQ calibration with longer prompts (include 512+ tokens) and post new calib files.
- Me (Olivia): schedule cross-variant eval (AWQ vs GPTQ-int8) on 1k eval set and report perf/accuracy tradeoffs.
Marcus: I'll drop the traces and the small repro job at `gs://redwood-perf/qwen-awq-1972345678/`.
Devon: if Marcus posts repro I'll try a local bisect on the selector cost model tomorrow AM.
Anya: also adding a transient flag to prefer `fast_gemm` for the affected pool as quick mitigation.
Marcus: thanks — will update thread when I have broader traces. :thumbsup:
